ORDER
PER HON’BLE MRS. SEEMA GUPTA, OFFICIATING CHAIRPERSON
IA NO. 626 OF 2026
(interim relief)
1. The present Interlocutory Application has been filed by Serentica
Renewables India 4 Pvt. Ltd. (“SRI4PL”/ “Appellant”) under Rule 30 of
the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (Procedure, Form, Fee, and Record
of Proceedings) Rules, 2007, seeking ex-parte ad-interim directions, in
the accompanying Appeal filed against the Central Electricity Regulatory
Commission (“CERC”/ “Central Commission”) and Central
Transmission Utility of India Ltd. (“CTUIL”/ “Respondent No. 2.”). The
Appeal challenges the common Order dated 02.03.2026 (“Impugned
Order”) passed by CERC in Petition No. 276/MP/2025 along with the
Page 2 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
connected matters in regard to the compensation cost levied towards
granting additional time for achieving commissioning of its 200MW Wind
Capacity Project located in Kallam, Maharashtra.
2. The Appellant has filed present application seeking following interim
reliefs: -
(a) Stay the operation of the Impugned Order dated 02.03.2026
passed by Ld. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission in Petition
No. 276/MP/2025, to the extent challenged by way of the present
Appeal, specifically directions to SRI4PL to make payments towards
penalty so as to retain its 200 MW Connectivity granted at Kallam SS,
as computed in terms of Paragraph 68 of the Impugned Order, till the
final disposal of the present Appeal;
(b) Stay the operation of the Demand Note dated 17.03.2026 raised
by CTUIL seeking payment of Rs 2,95,72,600/- by SRI4PL as well as
any future demands to be raised in terms of the Impugned Order, till
final disposal of the present Appeal;
(c) Stay the operation of Ld. CERC's direction that the validity of
SRI4PL's would be extended for a maximum period of 15 months
from 01.07.2025 as being arbitrary and without any basis and extend
the validity of the SRI4PL's connectivity till such time the Project is
commissioned;
(d) Direction to CTUIL to not take any coercive or punitive action
against SRI4PL further to the directions in the Impugned Order; and
e) Pass such other orders as this Hon'ble Tribunal deems fit.
Page 3 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
3. The Applicant has proposed to set up a 200 MW Wind Power Project
at Kallam, Maharashtra and had applied for stage-II Connectivity, vide
application dated 10.08.2022 with start date of connectivity and SCOD
from 01.07.2024. After notification of GNA Regulations, 2022, in terms of
Regulation 37, the Applicant filed the application dated 02.05.2023 for
transition of 200MW LTA/Connectivity from Connectivity Regulations,
2009 to GNA Regulations, 2022. On 01.03.2024 CTUIL intimated final
grant of connectivity for 200 MW, at Kallam SS, wherein the start date of
the connectivity was notified as 31.12.2024 subject to the availability of
Common Transmission System augmentation for connectivity under
GNA.
4. From 07.02.2025, CTUIL started raising invoices for transmission
charges in terms of Sharing Regulations, 2020. Subsequently, CTUIL
revoked SRI4PL’s connectivity vide its letter dated 10.03.2025 due to
failure in Commissioning of the project within timeline stipulated under
Regulation 24.6 (1)(a)(ii) i.e., by 30.12.2023 being 6 months from the
SCOD indicated in the connectivity application (30.06.2023).
5. Appellant had filed Petition No. 276/MP/2025 before CERC,
challenging the revocation of SRI4PL’s connectivity of 200 MW granted to
SRI4PL at Kallam SS in terms of Regulation 24.6(1)(a)(ii) of the GNA
Regulations, inter-alia, seeking the following reliefs: -(a) Quashing and
setting aside of two Notices dated 24.01.2025 issued by CTUIL to SRI4PL
(“Notices dated 24.01.2025”) in terms of Regulation 24.6(1)(a)(ii) of the
GNA Regulations, revoking the connectivity of 200 MWs granted to
SRI4PL;(b) Extension of the validity of the connectivity for 200 MW till
December 2025, or the actual date of commissioning, subject to grant of
statutory approvals required for commissioning the Project; (c) Exercise
Page 4 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
of CERC’s power to relax the applicability of Regulation 24.6(1)(a)(ii) of
the GNA Regulations such that validity of the connectivity granted to
SRI4PL is extended to enable SRI4PL commission the corresponding
wind capacity of 200 MW and utilize the said connectivity to evacuate
power.
6. By the Impugned Order, CERC, in exercise of powers under
Regulations 41 and 42 of the GNA Regulations, relaxed Regulation
24.6(1)(a)(ii) to permit retention of SRI4PL’s 200 MW Connectivity at
Kallam SS, subject to payment of compensation. CERC devised an
escalating compensation mechanism linked to Connectivity Bank
Guarantees (“Conn-BGs”) comprising upfront payment, daily charges,
and escalation up to 200%, subject to a maximum period of 15 months to
be recovered by CTUIL through adjustment of amounts recovered from
Conn-BG and by raising invoices for additional amounts till such time the
project is commissioned or expiry of the 15 months along with this, the
SRI4PL was directed to re-submit Conn-BGs which were returned in lieu
of the equivalent cash deposit by SRI4PL, within one month of the date of
the impugned order. CERC further held that for projects transitioning from
the Connectivity Regulations, 2009 to the GNA Regulations, SCOD shall
be the same as the start date sought in the transition application or the
start date granted by CTUIL in the grant of connectivity, whichever is later.
7. For SRI4PL, CERC had recognized a trigger date of 01.07.2025 and
even if part capacity achieves COD within this 3-month period, the amount
payable shall remain 50% of the total Conn-BGs without any pro-rata
refund (ii) the period beyond 3 months i.e. from the 3rd month till the 15th
month compensation mechanism was worked out.
Page 5 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
8. Pursuant to which, CTUIL issued a Demand Note dated 17.03.2026
computing total compensation assessed towards the delay in
commissioning of the project of Rs. 10,45,72,600/- (at Rs. 2,083/MW/day
for 200 MW). It is submitted by Applicant that an amount of Rs 10.45 Crore
has already been paid under protest, and approximately Rs 1.05 crores
towards bilateral Bills raised by CTUIL from 07.02.2025 till 01.07.2026 at
the rate of Rs 6,00,000 per month has been paid. Applicant/Appellant
has enclosed a table alongwith its written submissions detailing payments
paid as well as estimated compensation, according to which an total
potential liability amount works out to Rs. 19,63,22,600 up to 30.09.2026.
9. Aggrieved by the imposition of compensation charges and
extension of SCOD only up 30.09.2026, non-consideration of specific
force majeure events affecting the Applicant’s project, Appellant has filed
present Appeal as well as filed the subject application for interim relief, as
admittedly out of 200 MW capacity , only about 102.3 MW has been
commissioned and commissioning of balance capacity shall extend
beyond 30.09.2026, and there is threat of revocation of capacity for non-
commissioned capacity post 30.09.2026.
DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS
10. We have heard Mr. B.P Patil, Learned Senior Counsel appearing on
behalf of the Appellant/Applicant, Mr. Nikhil Nayyar, Learned Senior
Counsel appearing on behalf of the 2nd Respondent-CTUIL and Mr.
Dhananjay Baijal Counsel for the Commission and perused the written
submissions filed by parties, which are summarized hereunder, and other
documents on record:
Page 6 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
SUBMISSIONS URGED ON BEHALF OF APPELLANT
11. It is submitted on behalf of Applicant/Appellant that CERC failed to
consider force majeures for the subject project, in fixing the extension
period while at Paragraph 58 of the Impugned Order, CERC has
recognized, that the Project was affected by uncontrollable and
unforeseen events, however it returned no independent finding correlating
the 15-months outer limit to the actual delay caused by those events. It is
further pointed out that the 15 months extension time line in terms of
Impugned Order shall expire on 30.09.2026, and there is threat to
revocation of connectivity for the part capacity which is yet to be
commissioned. Applicant submits that SRI4PL has invested
approximately Rs. 2,512.25 Crore towards developing its Project and
about 102.3 MW has already been commissioned. Further, another 22
WTGs corresponding to 72.6 MW, has been erected and FTC (First Time
Charging approvals) approval have been received and another 2-3
months time is required for completion of pre-commissioning and
commissioning activities.
12. It is submitted that the Impugned Order failed to account for the
impact of force majeure events, brought on record by SRI4PL at the time
of adjudication of Petition No. 276/MP/2025, being: (a) Inordinate delay in
grant of statutory micro-siting approvals by MEDA, the Appellant submits
that from February 2023, it has applied for statutory approvals by MEDA
as SRI4PL cannot set up WTGs without confirmation of locations,
however the approvals were granted after a delay ranging from 20 days
to 1038 days. (b) unprecedented rainfall from July–October 2024 and
May–August 2025 in Osmanabad, Maharashtra, hampered Project works,
Page 7 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
as evinced by letters dated 15.01.2025 and 09.09.2025 from the District
Collector, Dharashiv (c) delay in PTCC approval for the 33kV internal
transmission network and 220kV DTL that SRI4PL filed PTCC approval
applications on 13.04.2024 but received approvals only on 27.03.2025
and (d) RoW issues, including agitation by farmers and political
intervention, hindering Project works and mitigating activities.
13. Applicant/Appellant further submits that post reserving the
Impugned Order, some events occurred, which were beyond SRI4PL's
control like an ongoing spate of theft and vandalism at the Project site
(33kV wiring/poles, WTG copper wiring, aluminium conductors,
transformer components), accompanied by threats to personnel. FIRs
have already been filed and representations have been made to the
District Collector and Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Since replacement parts
are sourced from OEMs in China and take 3–6 months, SRI4PL, in order
to reduce the timeline and to restore the affected WTGs delivered on site
but yet to be installed and submits that the installed WTGs may be
commissioned as per the timelines under FTC approvals. It is contented
that the magnitude of RoW issues in Maharashtra is evidences in the letter
dated 08.01.2025 to MNRE and MNRE letter to the Chief Minister of
Maharashtra dated 13.01.2025 and its response dated 06.03.2025.
Further, to mitigate this, on 04.02.2026, SRI4PL received anti-theft
charging approvals for 14 km DTL and has spent approximately Rs. 1.45
crore to deploy government security personnel of Maharashtra State
Security Corporation to address RoW issues and ensure safe working
conditions at the project site and spent Rs. 9.5 crore on CCTV/perimeter
detection system and sensors and security guards for patrolling.
Page 8 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
14. During hearing of the Interim application, Learned senior Counsel
for Applicant prays for extension of 3 months from 30.09.2026 (i.e., the
date on which connectivity can be revoked for non-commissioned
capacity) up to 31.12.2026, so as to overcome the delays caused due to
ongoing RoW issues of theft and vandalism, and commission the 22
WTGs corresponding to 72.6 MW wind capacity and the balance capacity,
without payment of any penalty for such 3-month extension and to
continue the interim protection granted vide Order dated 20.05.2026, till
final disposal of the present Appeal.
SUBMISSIONS URGED ON BEHALF OF RESPONDENT NO 2- CTUIL
15. Learned Senior Counsel submitted that by virtue of the Impugned
Order, the Central Commission not only extended the trigger date from
the original revocation date of 01.01.2025 to 01.07.2025 but also granted
a period of 15 months from the extended trigger date, i.e. from
01.07.2025, subject to the payment of compensation. Therefore, overall,
the Applicant has been granted 21 months to achieve commissioning of
its Project, i.e., by 30.09.2026. Having accepted and availed the benefit
of retention of connectivity, the Appellant cannot challenge the condition
attached to retention of Connectivity post the trigger date, i.e., the
payment of compensation. The said compensation mechanism ensures
that there is no squatting or retention of scarce ISTS resources in
perpetuity. CERC therefore, balanced competing interests by permitting
retention of connectivity while imposing compensation linked to Conn-BG
values. It is further submitted that the Applicant voluntarily opted for
transition and became a deemed applicant under the GNA regime, and
is accordingly bound by all the provisions of the GNA Regulations,
Page 9 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
including compliance with timelines, obligations and consequences
prescribed therein. Respondent No 2 submits that in case of
relinquishment, the grantee surrenders the connectivity and the
corresponding capacity is released to the system and the consequence is
one-time and capped to Conn-BGs. On the contrary, the compensation
mechanism as per the Impugned Order is the price of continued retention
of an unused scarce resource. The escalation in the compensation
mechanism is calibrated to the increasing cost of prolonged blockage and
operates so long as the Appellant chooses retention over the surrender
option. Further, CERC, in the Impugned Order has also recorded that
compensation to be paid for retention of connectivity shall have no bearing
on the liability under the Sharing Regulations, 2020. Therefore, the
Transmission charges applicable under the Sharing Regulations, 2020
are levied to recover the cost from users in a non-discriminatory manner.
Whereas the compensation mechanism imposed is linked to the delay and
arises solely on account of the Appellant's failure to commission its project
within prescribed timelines while continuing to retain allocated
connectivity.
16. Respondent No 2 further submits that CERC has considered the
alleged Force Majeure events and categorically recorded in Paragraph 61
that the Project is under an advanced stage of implementation where
mostly WTGs have been erected and the project should be allowed to be
commissioned, however further recorded that the Petitioners should have
taken advanced steps to complete their Projects within the timeline
provided under the regulation such that the transmission system is
optimally utilised. It was in the said circumstances that the Central
Commission exercised its power to relax and granted an extension subject
to compensation, with an outer limit of 15 months. Without prejudice to the
Page 10 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
above, as on date, 102.3 MW (out of 200 MW) stands commissioned.
Insofar as the 62.7 MW is concerned, the Appellant has placed on record
the letter dated 09.07.2026 issued by extending the period for injection of
infirm power up to 07.10.2026. As such, WRLDC is not the competent
authority to grant extension and is merely granting time for infirm power
injection. However, if this Tribunal is inclined to grant any limited relief, the
same may only be in respect of such 62.7 MW capacity and up to
07.10.2026, subject to payment of compensation in terms of the
mechanism prescribed under the Impugned Order for the period beyond
30.09.2026. It is further submitted that any such limited extension, if
granted, ought not to operate as a precedent and may be confined to the
peculiar facts of the present case, particularly where the capacity of 62.7
MW is stated to be ready for commissioning. The Appellant, however, has
not placed any materials regarding the balance 35 MW capacity.
Accordingly, the Connectivity corresponding to such 35 MW ought to be
revoked with effect from 01.10.2026.
17. It is submitted that in terms of Impugned Order, Applicant/Appellant
is liable to pay an amount of Rs. 20.33 crore, as on 30.09.2026, out of
which only Rs.10.45 crore has already been paid. In case this Hon'ble
Tribunal deems it fit to grant any further extension beyond 30.09.2026, the
Applicant/Appellant ought to be directed to deposit the entire
compensation amount of Rs. 20.33 crore, along with compensation for the
extension beyond 30.09.2026 (if any) granted by this Tribunal.
OUR CONSIDERATION
18. After hearing the learned senior counsel for the parties, the principal
issue arising for consideration in the present application is the threat of
Page 11 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
revocation of connectivity for the non-commissioned capacity post
30.09.2026 in terms of the Impugned Order. The Applicant has also
prayed for stay of the balance compensation payment directed therein.
19. By way of the Impugned Order, petitions filed by three generators
concerning non-commissioning of their respective projects on account of
various difficulties, including force majeure, and seeking extension of time
for commissioning, were disposed of. The submissions of the
Applicant/Appellant, are recorded at page 7 onwards of the Impugned
Order, which specifically advert to the force majeure conditions faced by
them as well as their submissions that the entire 350 MW capacity is likely
to be commissioned by December 2026, with 263 MW expected by June
2026. The petition of the Applicant/Appellant before CERC was confined
to connectivity for 200 MW of project capacity. In terms of the Impugned
Order, the Connectivity Revocation date of 01.01.2025 for 200 MW project
capacity of Appellant, was extended to 01.07.2025, under Issue No1.
20. Under Issue No 2, CERC takes note that Regulation 24.6 of the
GNA Regulations mandates revocation of connectivity after six months
from the scheduled date of commercial operation, however, considering
the force majeure conditions faced by the projects and noting that projects
were at an advanced stage of construction, observed that revocation at
this stage would not be prudent in the sector’s interest, though it also
emphasized that petitioners ought to have taken timely steps to complete
their projects.
21. Considering the submissions made by the Petitioners, including the
Appellant herein and taking note of status of installation of WTG and
transmission line, CERC thought it to be a fit case to exercise its power to
Page 12 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
relax and remove difficulty and for revocation of their Regulatory power to
safeguard the interest of the sector. However, it was further observed that
the Petitioners are holding the scarce resource and have not been able to
complete the project within specified time line under the Regulation, such
relaxation should be subject to payment of compensation.
22. Thereafter, CERC utilizing its power under Regulation 41 (Power to
relax) and Regulation 42 (Power to remove Difficulty) under GNA
Regulations relaxed the Regulation 24.6 of the GNA Regulations to the
extent that connectivity shall not be revoked under Regulation 24.6 of the
GNA Regulations by CTUIL and worked out a methodology for the
compensation. A maximum time extension of 15 months was granted for
achieving the SCOD from the Trigger date i.e., 01.07.2025 with varying
compensation mechanism.
23. In the case of the Appellant/Applicant, retention of connectivity
beyond the trigger date of 01.07.2025 has been permitted for an extended
period of fifteen months, albeit subject to payment of compensation in
terms of the Impugned Order. At this ad-interim stage, we are unable to
accept the contention of the Appellant/Applicant that the Impugned Order
has failed to deliberate upon the force majeure conditions urged by them
and that a blanket extension of fifteen months has been granted. On the
contrary, we find that the CERC, in the Impugned Order, has duly taken
cognizance of the force majeure issues faced by the Appellant/Applicant’s
project. It is also significant that the Appellant/Applicant itself has
submitted that its project is expected to be commissioned by June 2026,
whereas the SCOD has been extended up to September 2026, i.e., three
months beyond the Appellant’s own projection. In these circumstances,
we do not consider it appropriate, at this ad-interim stage, to stay the
Page 13 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
operation of the Impugned Order on this ground. This observation is,
however, made without prejudice to the rival contentions of the parties on
the aforesaid aspect, which shall be examined at the time of final hearing
of the Appeal.
24. Applicant/ Appellant has made submissions before us, that
subsequent to reserving of the Impugned Order by CERC, there has been
delay in achieving the commissioning on account of theft and vandalism,
which are being addressed by them expeditiously. We are of the view that
such developments ought to have been brought to the notice of CERC
prior to pronouncement of Impugned Order. Nevertheless, at the interim
stage, considering that Applicant is praying for a further time period of
three months only, it may not be prudent to let the connectivity be revoked
after completion of extension period i.e., by 30.09.2026 in terms of
Impugned Order especially when FTC for the 72.6 MW capacity has been
achieved, though Respondent No 2 contended it to be for 62.7 MW, which
we do not find necessary to adjudicate at this stage, and the said 72.6
MW capacity is expected to be commissioned by December 2026.
Accordingly, we are of the view that the Applicant/Appellant made out a
prima facie case and balance of convenience lie in the favour of Applicant
for grant of some interim relief.
25. Insofar as compensation is concerned, we take note that extension
in commissioning of the project beyond the time line stipulated in the
applicable Regulations has been granted in the Impugned Order in
exercise of power under Regulation 41 ( Power to relax) and Regulation
42 (Power to Remove Difficulty) and compensation has been worked
considering that connectivity is a scarce resource and applicant has not
been able to commission the project, accordingly we are not inclined to
Page 14 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
interfere with compensation methodology indicated in the Impugned
Order at the Interim Stage as the issue needs detailed deliberations which
can be taken up at the time of hearing of the main Appeal after going
through the Regulation and rival contentions. Applicant in its written
submissions has admitted the potential liability of compensation as Rs
19,63,22,600 in terms of Impugned order up to 30.09.2026, in which Rs
10,45,72,600 has already been paid by Applicant, albeit under protest,
and balance potential liability is of Rs 9,17,50,000. While Respondent
No 2 has contended that total liability amount works out to Rs 20.33 Crore
upto 30.09.2026, and any Interim Relief should be subject to payment of
balance amount in Rs 20.33Crore after considering payment of Rs 10.45
Crore already made and further it should also be subject to the payment
of compensation for the extended period, if granted by this Tribunal. At
the Interim Stage, we don’t feel it necessary to adjudicate the exact
amount payable up to 30.09.2026 as well as the amount of compensation
for the extended period, same shall be deliberated at the time of hearing
of the main Appeal.
26. The rival contentions of the parties on other grounds raised in the
Appeal, are left open and shall be considered and adjudicated at the time
of final hearing of the main Appeal and nothing in this order shall be
construed as a finding on the merits of those contentions.
27. In view of above deliberations, we extend the SCOD for a further
period of three months from 30.09.2026 i.e. up to 31.12.2026 for the 72.6
MW capacity, for which FTC has been approved. Further, such
extension, shall be subject to the payment of balance amount of Rs
9,17,50,000 to CTUIL by the Appellant/Applicant within two weeks of date
of this order, failing which the CTUIL would be at the liberty to revoke the
Page 15 of 16

Order in IA No. 626 of 2026 in Appeal No. 142 of 2026
connectivity for the capacity not commissioned out of the 72.6 MW by that
date. We however make it clear that the compensation, if any, for the
extended period in terms of this order, as well as the compensation
amount already paid and payable as directed above to CTUIL by the
Appellant /Applicant shall be subject to the outcome of the Appeal.
28. The IA No. 626 of 2026 is disposed of in these terms.
APPEAL NO. 142 OF 2026
It is to note that reply has not been filed by the 1st Respondent
despite opportunity given vide earlier orders dated 01.07.2026 &
15.07.2026. Respondent no.2 has already filed reply, against which
rejoinder has also been filed by the Appellant, therefore, pleadings qua
Respondent No.2 are complete.
Registry is directed to include this matter in the ‘List of Finals’, to
be taken up, in its turn.
PRONOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON THIS 23rd DAY OF
SEPTEMBER, 2026.
(Virender Bhat) (Seema Gupta)
Judicial Member Officiating Chairperson
